Massachusetts commercial solar incentives

Our current data does not list Massachusetts commercial solar incentives. It shows where solar fits in our growth plan and in one open bid, but not program names, rates or eligibility rules. We won't guess at them here.

What our data covers

  • Solar is a Phase 3 service line. Our growth plan lists solar and storage O&M with SCADA monitoring, EV depot charging and NuWave efficiency. These services are meant to turn one-off bids into recurring contracts (CET growth plan).
  • Recurring work is the goal. The growth plan targets a ~25% recurring service mix by month 36. That figure is a labelled assumption, not guidance (CET growth plan).
  • One open bid includes renewables. The Massport Worcester Regional Airport 149A trade-contractor RFQ covers electrical upgrades, fire alarm, lighting and "renewable energy upgrades." It was due Oct 8, 2026 (CET opportunity radar).
  • Some state sources were not itemized. Several Massachusetts procurement and funding sites blocked automated access, including mass.gov and COMMBUYS. The radar's coverage of Massachusetts programs is incomplete (CET opportunity radar).

# Massachusetts commercial solar incentives

**Our current data does not list Massachusetts commercial solar incentives.** It shows where solar fits in our growth plan and in one open bid, but not program names, rates or eligibility rules. We won't guess at them here.

## What our data covers

- **Solar is a Phase 3 service line.** Our growth plan lists solar and storage O&M with SCADA monitoring, EV depot charging and NuWave efficiency. These services are meant to turn one-off bids into recurring contracts (CET growth plan).
- **Recurring work is the goal.** The growth plan targets a ~25% recurring service mix by month 36. That figure is a labelled assumption, not guidance (CET growth plan).
- **One open bid includes renewables.** The Massport Worcester Regional Airport 149A trade-contractor RFQ covers electrical upgrades, fire alarm, lighting and "renewable energy upgrades." It was due Oct 8, 2026 (CET opportunity radar).
- **Some state sources were not itemized.** Several Massachusetts procurement and funding sites blocked automated access, including mass.gov and COMMBUYS. The radar's coverage of Massachusetts programs is incomplete (CET opportunity radar).

## What our data does not cover

| Question | Status in our data | Source that would answer it |
|---|---|---|
| State solar incentive programs | Not covered | Massachusetts energy agency program rules and current tariffs |
| Federal tax credits | Not covered | Current federal tax-credit guidance for commercial solar |
| Utility incentives and interconnection | Not covered | Program schedules from each local utility |
| Incentive value per project | Not covered | Program rate tables applied to sample CET project sizes |

We don't give tax, legal or regulatory-compliance advice. Owners should confirm eligibility with their own advisors.

## Why incentives matter for bids

- Incentives can change project economics for commercial owners, and that affects how much solar work gets built (est.).
- Solar O&M contracts that come out of installs would support the recurring mix in our growth plan (est.).
- None of this has been sized. We have no solar pipeline count or dollar value for Massachusetts.

Incentive terms decide whether solar becomes repeat O&M revenue or stays a few one-off installs, and that service mix is what moves CET's exit multiple.

## Next actions

1. **Build an incentive brief.** Pull current Massachusetts and federal commercial solar program terms into the opportunity radar, with sources and dates.
2. **Pull state data by hand.** Retrieve Massachusetts listings from the sites that blocked automated access, starting with COMMBUYS, and tag solar and storage items.
3. **Check the Worcester airport bid.** Confirm whether the Oct 8, 2026 submission went in, and how much of it is renewable energy scope.
4. **Size the O&M opportunity.** Estimate how many installed systems near Worcester, Taunton and Norwell could become service contracts, and label the result as an estimate.
